summary.headline: Smartworks Q1 FY27 revenue rose 44% YoY to INR 546 crores, with normalized EBITDA margin at 19.6% and guidance of 28-30% revenue growth reaffirmed.
summary.overview: Revenue reached INR 546 crores, up 44% YoY and 5% QoQ, while normalized EBITDA grew 74% YoY to INR 107 crores at a 19.6% margin. Normalized PAT nearly tripled YoY to INR 39 crores. Growth was supported by mature-centre occupancy (committed 92%) and a higher share of 1,000+ seat clients, GCCs and multi-city clients, though overall occupancy dipped to 81% from 82% QoQ as new centres filled up. Management reaffirmed FY27 guidance (28-30% revenue growth, 19-20% normalized EBITDA margin, 13 million sq ft by March 2027) and started a heavy capex cycle of INR 550-600 crores for the year.

vs negative INR 4.9 crores a year ago
vs INR 22 crores in same quarter last year

segments.name: Core rental (enterprise annuity)
segments.commentary: Enterprise annuity demand is 92% of rental revenue; 1,000+ seat cohort is 41% of revenue (37% in FY26). Committed contracted revenue is about INR 5,400 crores, covering 87% of FY27 revenue.

segments.name: GCC clients
segments.commentary: GCCs contribute 21% of revenue, up from 15% in FY26. Recent wins include a Swiss bank and a manufacturing GCC; a Japanese NBFC subsidiary took space in Mumbai.

segments.name: Singapore
segments.commentary: Work Studio acquired, taking the portfolio to over 1,500 seats (about 2% of revenue); 400-450 seats now available to sell, funded from Singapore cash flows. Management says no further meaningful expansion planned.

segments.name: Value-added services (VAS)
segments.commentary: Non-lease rental revenue rose to over INR 68 crores from INR 22 crores YoY, and is take-rate based with no direct cost. VAS guidance is not built into the FY27 projections.

guidance_outlook: Reaffirmed FY27 revenue growth of 28-30%, normalized EBITDA margin of 19-20%, and operational footprint above 13 million sq ft by March 2027.
Plans to add 2.5-3 million sq ft of operational space in FY27; more than 3.5 million sq ft signed, giving a buffer of about 0.7-0.8 million sq ft.
Capex guided at INR 550-600 crores for FY27, with heavy spend in the next two quarters.
Management expects ROCE to expand meaningfully through FY28 as capex cohorts mature.
Revenue jump expected mainly in Q3 or Q4 as new centres ramp up (about 12 months to ramp).
capex_capacity: Operational footprint 10.4 million sq ft as of June 2026; 1.9 million sq ft under fit-out; 0.3 million sq ft added in Q1 and 2.1 million sq ft over the last 12 months.

About 3 million sq ft to come online over the next 9 months, including Eastbridge (Mumbai) and Eastside (Pune), both landing in H2 FY27. Vikhroli asset is 8.15 lakh sq ft, described as the world's largest standalone managed campus.
New fit-out capex is INR 1,350 per sq ft, rising about 5% a year; refurbishment is about 15% of initial capex every three years (around INR 5 per sq ft per year, by management's estimate).
Every building needed for the next two years is secured; FY29 work has begun. Long-term rights give 10-15 years of access.
Security deposits of INR 33 crores paid to landlords to lock buildings for FY28 and part of FY29.
demand_pricing: Occupancy 81% (vs 82% in Q4 FY26), reflecting new centres still filling. Mature centres at 89% on 9.1 million sq ft; committed occupancy 92%. Management guides 80-85% occupancy over the next three quarters.

Seat retention 74% in Q1, with client count down while occupied seats and revenue rose. Management says the churn is deliberate repricing of older, lower-rate clients; the annual retention range it cited was 80-88%.
Realization on incremental mature-footprint seats leased in Q1 FY27 was about INR 181 per sq ft per month, up from about INR 170 a year earlier. Management cited a rental INR 185 per seat figure.
Mix: IT/ITES down to 35% of clients (from over 40%); target 25-30/35%. Multi-city clients 35% of revenue (31% in FY26).
Pre-commitment: about 30-35% of new buildings is pre-committed by existing or incoming clients. Landlord mix is about 65% non-institutional and 35% institutional.

qa_highlights.question: Rationale for the Singapore Work Studio acquisition, expected revenue and occupancy, and whether fit-out costs of INR 1,350 face inflation.
qa_highlights.answer: Acquired from internal cash flows at roughly construction cost; the target was about 60% occupied. Singapore is about 80,000 sq ft in total and 2% of revenue, with 400-450 seats now available to sell. Expansion will not be meaningful, and capex is set at INR 550-600 crores for FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the expansion is speculative, and how much is pre-leased?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 30-35% of any new building is pre-committed by existing clients, and occupancy ramps to 80-85% within 13-14 months, as seen on prior centres.

qa_highlights.question: Is the drop in retention a sign of demand weakness, and will similar churn continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 74% was Q2-seasonal churn; mature committed occupancy is 92%, and most churned space is already re-let. Churn is expected to fall in Q3 and Q4, as in prior years.

qa_highlights.question: Is there supply risk from developer delays?
qa_highlights.answer: Supply is covered by a buffer of 0.7-0.8 million sq ft over the 2.5-3 million sq ft target, and management is working with institutional developers such as DLF, Hiranandani, Tata, Panchshil and Salarpuria.

qa_highlights.question: How is the 28-30% guidance built, given the existing base is at 92% committed occupancy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the base is almost fully sold, so growth depends on new centres that take about 12 months to ramp. Growth is expected to show mainly in Q3 or Q4, and the range is one management is confident about.

qa_highlights.question: Why did OCF/EBITDA dip, and what about VAS margins and pricing power?
qa_highlights.answer: The dip reflects INR 33 crores of security deposits paid to landlords. VAS is take-rate based with no direct cost, so it is margin accretive, but it is only in pilot stages and not in FY27 projections. Management said the nearest competitor prices 10-15% higher than Smartworks.

risks_watch: Occupancy may stay at 80-85% in the next three quarters as large new centres ramp, and it could drop further.
Revenue guidance depends on new-centre ramp-up and handover timing, with most of the uplift in Q3-Q4 FY27.
Capex of INR 550-600 crores is front-loaded; FCF is negative (INR -56 crores in Q1) and depends on OCF recovering after deposit payments.
IT/ITES share is falling, and management could not give a call-centre (AI-exposed) breakdown.
Retention of 74% in Q1 needs to recover in the seasonally stronger H2 to validate the 80-88% annual range management cited.
Revenue and EBITDA margin depend on keeping the 19-20% range while absorbing new cohorts.
Management corrected several numbers during the call (Singapore occupancy, seat count, IT/ITES share, retention), so the transcript figures should be checked against the presentation.
summary.management_tone: Confident and promotional. Management was emphatic about visibility, compounding margins and supply security. It was more defensive on retention (74%), the OCF/EBITDA dip, and the Q1 occupancy decline, which it attributed to new centres and deliberate repricing.
key_quotes: We don't manage for the quarter; we are building for the decade.
Fewer, bigger, longer-duration clients - that is by design.
